Raise against evidence, not narrative

By lowob · 12 February 2026 · 3-minute read · Strategy

In short: investors price risk. Narrative asks them to imagine the risk away; evidence removes some of it. Even a small amount of real evidence changes which investors take the call, how fast they move and what they ask for.

Key points

  • At pre-seed, investors weight founder–market fit, a sharp problem, and five to ten named people who would use it.
  • In web3, points and incentive campaigns produce numbers that look like adoption until the incentive stops.
  • In AI, a demo proves the model can do something once; investors want a customer letting it do the job daily.
  • An evidence log records usage, quotes, commitments, community work and lost deals, each dated and specific.
  • Without evidence yet, raise less from idea-stage backers or spend four to six weeks getting first evidence.

Not investment or legal advice. lowob advises on narrative and readiness; it doesn't arrange, value or negotiate rounds.

What counts as evidence at each stage

Stage Evidence investors weight most Usually not enough on its own
Pre-seed Founder–market fit, a sharp problem, 5–10 named people who'd use it Follower counts, a waitlist nobody has been asked to act on
Seed Design partners or pilots with usage, early retention, a few paying users Testnet activity driven by points or airdrops
Series A Repeatable acquisition, revenue or fees that recur, a channel that scales One big logo with no expansion

In web3, the trap is activity that was paid for. Points programs and incentive campaigns produce numbers that look like adoption until the incentive stops. Sophisticated investors now strip them out, so you should strip them out first and show what's left.

In AI, the trap is the demo. A good demo proves the model can do something once. Investors want to see that a customer let it do the job every day.

Building the evidence log

Keep one running document. Every entry is dated and specific.

  • Usage: who used it, how often, for what.
  • Quotes: what a user said, in their words, with permission to reuse.
  • Commitments: pilots, LOIs, integrations, partnerships with a named counterpart.
  • Community work: contributions, referrals, content made by people you didn't pay.
  • Losses: deals you lost and why. Investors trust a founder who knows why they lose.

This log is also your customer case-study source and your community recognition list. It's the first shared asset between the three workstreams from Part 1.

Rewriting the deck around it

Move your best evidence to slide 2 or 3, before the market slide. Then let the market slide answer the question the evidence raised: if this one buyer wants it, how many more are there?

The vision slide gets shorter. Evidence does the work vision was doing.

When you don't have any yet

Then the honest move is to raise less, from people who back founders at the idea stage, or to spend four to six weeks getting the first evidence before you go out. One design partner using the product weekly is worth more than another month of deck revisions.

The checklist

  • [ ] Three things a non-founder has done with the product, written down
  • [ ] Incentivised activity separated from organic activity
  • [ ] An evidence log that's updated weekly
  • [ ] Best evidence on slide 2 or 3
  • [ ] A clear answer to: what does this round prove next?

Common questions

What evidence do investors want at seed stage?

Design partners or pilots with usage, early retention, and a few paying users. Testnet activity driven by points or airdrops is usually not enough on its own.

Where should traction go in a pitch deck?

Move your best evidence to slide 2 or 3, before the market slide, then let the market slide answer how many more buyers like this one there are. The vision slide gets shorter.

What should I do if I have no traction before fundraising?

Raise less, from people who back founders at the idea stage, or spend four to six weeks getting the first evidence before going out. One design partner using the product weekly is worth more than another month of deck revisions.
